name: Cool Head
tagline: Anger that doesn't wreck your relationships
about: Cool Head helps you get through the hot moment, log what set you off, find the pattern behind your anger, and repair after you've said something you regret.
persona: You are a non-judgemental anger coach: anger is information, not a character flaw; you focus on the gap between feeling and action, and you say plainly when anger has tipped into risk to others.

onboarding.title: Turn heat into information
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where anger tends to show up for you.

tools.title: Cool down now
tools.subtitle: Ninety seconds before you act

inputs.label: What just happened
inputs.placeholder: he interrupted me again in front of everyone

tools.prompt: Heat: {level}. Trigger: {trigger}. Steps for the next 90 seconds with exact timings (exit, body, breath, one sentence), a quote with the exact line to say to buy time without escalating, and a callout on the sign that it's not safe to stay in the room.

tools.title: Log an episode
tools.subtitle: Trigger → thought → action → cost

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: kids ignored me three times, I shouted, everyone cried, felt awful

tools.prompt: Log this episode: {episode} (it ended: {outcome}). Kv (Trigger, Hot thought, Underlying need, Action, Cost), a table (Earlier exit point | What it could have looked like), bullets on the one thing to try next time the same trigger appears, and a callout urging professional help if episodes involve threats or physical contact.

tools.title: Find my patterns
tools.subtitle: Paste several entries

inputs.label: Your log entries
inputs.placeholder: Mon: traffic, cut off, shouted alone… Wed: partner's tone…

tools.prompt: Analyse these entries: {entries}. Table (Pattern | Triggers | Time of day or state | Frequency), bullets on the two conditions that make anger most likely (hunger, sleep, feeling unheard, etc.), steps for a 2-week experiment targeting the top condition, and a callout on how to know if it's working.

tools.title: Repair after blowing up
tools.subtitle: Own it without grovelling

inputs.label: What you did or said
inputs.placeholder: yelled that she never listens and slammed the door

tools.prompt: Write a repair for {who} after this: {said}. Quote with what to say (under 100 words, ownership without excuses, no 'but'), steps for the conversation including what to do if they're not ready, bullets on the follow-through that proves it, and a callout on what not to do (over-apologising, gifts instead of change).

tools.title: Say it without heat
tools.subtitle: Turn a rant into a request

inputs.label: The rant version
inputs.placeholder: I'm sick of being the only one who cleans anything in this house

tools.prompt: Convert this rant into an assertive request: {rant}. Quote with the assertive version (observation, feeling, need, one specific ask), a table (Rant phrase | Assertive phrase | Why it lands better), and bullets on the best timing and place to say it.

disclaimer: Not therapy or medical advice. If you're in crisis or thinking about harming yourself or someone else, contact local emergency services or a crisis line now. If anger has become physical, seek help from a professional or a domestic-abuse service.
